title: Define eval contracts and rollback metrics for Optimize
creator: Ravi Patel
description:
Problem: Optimize needs a precise, testable contract for model and optimization changes so we can ship quantization/quant configs, model swaps, and prompt-based caching improvements without unexpected user regressions. This ticket defines the eval surface area (prompt sets and coverage), regression thresholds, A/B test pass/fail logic, and automated rollback triggers that the product, applied-ML, and SRE teams will enforce before and after rollout.

Goal: Provide a single source-of-truth acceptance policy for Optimize releases that balances sensitivity (catch bad regressions quickly) with noise reduction (avoid unnecessary rollbacks for statistical variance). The contract must be automatable, auditable, and integrate into existing CI/CD, datadog/observability dashboards, and the rollout console.
background: Previous incidents in runtime-1.18 and earlier Optimize experiments showed subtle semantic regressions after model swaps and a 2-3x spike in tail latency when certain batching heuristics changed. Past gating relied on small human eval sets and ad-hoc thresholds. We need a repeatable, measurable approach for v2 that matches Redwood's production-first thesis. This ties to the Optimize product workstream to expose quantization recommendations and automated rollout controls.
success_metrics: Detect >90% of high-severity regressions (customer-visible hallucination or broken structured output) within 24h of deployment
False positive rollback rate <5% (alerts that lead to rollback but later determined to be non-actionable)
Mean composite quality score drop across release <= 2% relative to baseline
Critical customer flows (NPS sample) unchanged within 1.5% post-release
prompt_sets: seed-prod-regression-suite-v2: 250 canonical prompts covering summarization, instruction-following, extraction, code-gen, conversational turn-taking, and structured JSON outputs. Each prompt tagged by intent and difficulty.
safety-edgecase-set-v1: 120 adversarial prompts focusing on safety, policy boundary, and hallucination checks (used for blocking failures).
customer-spotlight-20: 20 prompts provided by large customers under NDA (sensitive coverage for Dedicated/Private customers).
latency-under-load-bench: 100 synthetic requests to measure P95/P99 tail latency with batching and KV-cache hot-paths simulated.
regression_thresholds: Composite quality score (CQS) drop > 2.0% absolute across seed-prod-regression-suite-v2 -> FAIL
Per-prompt failure rate increase > 5 percentage points for more than 10 prompts of highest priority -> FAIL
Semantic-similarity (embedding cosine) average drop > 0.035 on summarization/extraction prompts -> FAIL
Safety-edgecase: any single blocking safety prompt that moves from pass->fail triggers immediate human review and blocks rollout
P95 latency increase > 20% relative to baseline OR P99 increase > 15% with throughput unchanged -> FAIL
ab_test_criteria: Design: standard randomized A/B (control = current serving config, treatment = candidate config) with allocation ramping: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% over 72h windows (must hold each step for at least 12h and meet gating checks before next ramp).

Statistical: target sample size min N=5,000 user sessions or 100k tokens processed per arm, whichever is larger. Tests require p < 0.05 for primary metric with two-tailed test. For business-critical guardrails we use one-tailed tests where direction is explicit.
Primary metric: composite quality score (CQS) computed from weighted combination of automated similarity (40%), human micro-eval (40%), and safety checks (20%).
Secondary metrics: latency P95, error rate, token-cost per response, structured-output correctness (schema conformance).

Stopping rules: if treatment hits a FAIL according to regression_thresholds OR shows sustained statistically significant degradation on any primary or safety metric for 3 consecutive hours, pause ramp and trigger rollback path.
rollback_triggers: Immediate automated rollback if Safety-edgecase set has any blocking failure (binary).
Auto-rollback if composite quality score drop > 3.0% for a continuous 6-hour window and confirmed by automated checks (redundant metric computation).
Auto-rollback if P99 latency increases > 25% for 2 consecutive hours during normal traffic conditions (not during known infra incidents).
Manual rollback recommended (requires on-call + PM approval) if customer-facing error rate increase > 1% absolute for > 12h and requests from top 10 customers are affected.
Abort deployment (do not continue ramp) if initial 1% launch exceeds any FAIL criteria in the first 30 minutes.
runbook_actions: Alert channels: PagerDuty on-call (SRE), #optimize-release Slack channel, and PM/Applied-ML leads tagged.
Immediate steps: pause traffic ramp, snapshot candidate logs, switch traffic to control or previous stable release, open incident ticket in Jira/Linear linking PM-6128.
Investigation: Applied-ML triage for model-output differences, SRE triage for latency/infra causes, Eng to review kernel/quant changes (link PRs).
Mitigation: short-term rollback to previous release, enable fallback model-variant if available, and communicate to affected customers via status page and account teams.
Postmortem: within 5 business days include root cause, timeline, corrective actions, and follow-up tickets (owners assigned).
acceptance_criteria: All prompt_sets are checked into the Optimize eval repo and referenced by CI with stable identifiers (no ad-hoc local files).
Regression thresholds implemented as automated checks in the release pipeline and wired to Datadog/Prometheus dashboards with documented alerts.
A/B experiment scaffolding supports ramp policy, sample sizing controls, and automatic stop/rollback rules as described above.
Automation: new-change runs full eval suite in preprod and posts results to the rollout console with delta visualizations; human micro-eval queue created for ambiguous failures.
Documentation: PRD and runbook published to Confluence; release checklist includes signoffs from PM, Applied-ML, and SRE.
Stakeholder signoff: at least two reviewers from Applied-ML and one SRE have approved the gating logic and alert thresholds.
decisions: Use a hybrid composite quality score (CQS) combining automated embedding similarity and limited human micro-eval. Rationale: automated checks scale, human evals catch nuanced errors; weighted 40/40/20 (automated/human/safety).
Blocking safety prompts are binary gates (fail=block). Decision made after consultation with Safety and Legal teams to minimize user harm.
Latency and cost guardrails are part of the same gating system because Optimize changes often trade accuracy for cost; both dimensions need to be observable and actionable before rollout.
tradeoffs: Stricter thresholds reduce risk but increase false positives and slower release cadence.
Relying on human micro-eval improves precision but adds latency to preprod checks; we mitigate by sampling and parallelization.
Large A/B sample sizes increase confidence but delay rollouts; we use staged ramps to balance safety and speed.

open_questions: How do we version prompt sets in a way that is auditable and reproducible across private deployments (on-prem customers)?
What is the target cadence for re-running the safety-edgecase set during long-running canaries to avoid alert fatigue?
Should we permit soft-fail for low-priority prompts (log-only) to reduce false positives, and how to label those in the console?
